stories.text: As a client team member, I want to start a work item from Jira or Slack, so I don’t need a new tool.

acs.text: A Jira comment that mentions the flow on a configured project creates one work item linked to the issue
A Slack mention in a configured channel creates one work item and replies with its link
The same comment or mention delivered twice creates only one work item
A request from an unconfigured project or channel is refused and logged

stories.text: As a delivery lead, I want each work item to go through defined stages (spec → plan → implement → review → deploy), so AI work follows our SDLC.

acs.text: A new work item starts at the first stage of its configured flow
An agent stage launches a Claude Code run with the pinned context bundle and records its start and end
The agent’s claim of what it produced is checked (artifact hash) before the work item moves on
After a service restart, in-flight work items resume from their last recorded state

stories.text: As an approver, I want to approve or send back a stage’s output, so nothing moves forward without a named person deciding.

acs.text: A gate stops the flow and creates a pending approval for the configured role
Approve moves the work item to the next stage; send back returns it to the previous stage with a reason
The person who triggered or produced the work can’t approve their own gate
An approval that passes its SLA is flagged as overdue and the approver is notified
An approver can understand what they’re approving from the gate screen alone, without opening the repo

stories.text: As an agent, I want to ask a person a question mid-run, so I don’t have to guess.

acs.text: An agent question creates an escalation visible to the assigned person
The answer is passed back to the agent run and recorded
Repeated questions that don’t move the work forward are capped and escalated to the lead

stories.text: As an auditor, I want an Evidence Pack per work item, so I can see who decided what, when, and on what basis.

acs.text: Every stage start, end, gate decision and escalation is written to an append-only event log
The Evidence Pack lists each decision with its actor, timestamp, the artifact it was made against, and that artifact’s hash
Altering a recorded event is detectable (integrity chain or anchor check fails)
Evidence is stored in write-once storage with locked retention
The exported Evidence Pack is readable by a non-engineer auditor

stories.text: As an approver or lead, I want one dashboard to see work items, pending approvals and evidence.

acs.text: Only signed-in internal accounts can access the dashboard
The dashboard lists pending approvals for the signed-in user, oldest first
A work item page shows its timeline of stages, decisions and escalations
The dashboard is usable on a laptop screen without horizontal scrolling

stories.text: As a delivery lead, I want approved changes merged and deployed to the client’s environment, with the result recorded.

acs.text: After final approval, the PR is merged and the deploy stage runs
The deploy result (pass or fail, SHA) is recorded as evidence; a failed deploy opens an escalation
The GitHub connector passes the shared connector testkit
